image_description: A group of five people posing indoors with two bassoons. The person on the far left holds a disassembled or partially assembled bassoon horizontally. The woman on the far right holds a fully assembled bassoon vertically, resting the butt on the floor/seat and holding the upper joint. The instrument is tall, wooden, with metal keys. There is a grey case standing between them.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Long wooden wind instrument of considerable height when assembled.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The instrument held by the woman on the right is clearly very tall, extending from her lap to well above her head, consistent with the ~1.3m height of a bassoon.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Distinctive U-shape when viewed from front with bell pointing upward.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vertical instrument shows the characteristic double-tube structure (boot joint at bottom, wing joint and bell joint at top) creating a U-profile. The bell points upward.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Conical bore that doubles back on itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The internal bore structure is not visible from the exterior; this is an internal feature inferred from the external shape but not directly testable visually.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Curved metal bocal mouthpiece tube at top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A curved metal tube (bocal) is visible protruding from the top of the wing joint on the vertical instrument.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Numerous metal keys and tone holes distributed along length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Silver-colored keywork is clearly visible along the length of both instruments, particularly on the lower joint and boot joint.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bell flares outward at top and instrument held diagonally across body when played.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bell at the top of the vertical instrument flares correctly. While not currently being 'played' in a performance sense, the hold is consistent with how the instrument is supported (diagonal/vertical orientation relative to the player).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dark reddish-brown polished wood finish maple or rosewood.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The wood has the characteristic dark reddish-brown hue and polished sheen associated with maple bassoons.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Metal keys are silver or gold-plated.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The keys appear silver/nickel-silver in color, reflecting light appropriately.
The main body segments are clearly constructed from turned wood.

artifact_observations.location: T-shirt of the woman in the center
artifact_observations.reasoning: The text on the black t-shirt is illegible and distorted, resembling AI-generated pseudo-text rather than clear typography. It looks like 'G... something...'. This is a common artifact in generative images involving text.

artifact_observations.location: Hands of the woman on the right holding the bassoon
artifact_observations.reasoning: The fingers wrapping around the instrument look slightly fused and lack distinct knuckle definition. The grip appears physically weak or anatomically ambiguous, typical of AI struggles with complex hand-object interactions.

artifact_observations.location: Face of the man on the far left
artifact_observations.reasoning: The skin texture is overly smooth and plastic-like compared to the rest of the image, lacking fine pore detail, suggesting slight generative smoothing.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific taxonomic classification of the instrument as a bassoon and distinguish it from similar woodwinds like the contrabassoon or oboe.
To verify that the complex keywork is physically attached to the wooden body and not floating or melting into the wood, which is a high-risk area for AI generation.
To closely inspect the anatomical correctness of the hands holding the instrument and the facial features, checking for subtle distortions missed by the router.
To analyze the illegible text on the central figure's shirt to determine if it is gibberish or just low-resolution compression artifacts.

focus_areas: Keywork connectivity: Ensure every key has a logical rod/post connection to the wood.
Hand anatomy: Verify finger count and joint articulation on the hands gripping the instrument.
Bocal insertion: Check if the bocal inserts cleanly into the wing joint without melting.
Text legibility: Assess the nature of the distortion on the clothing.
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'text_gibberish' artifact. In real photos, text might be blurry due to focus/compression, but AI text often has character-level structural failures (impossible glyphs). Differentiate between optical blur and generative failure. Also, scrutinize the 'structural_collapse' of the hands; AI often merges fingers when they wrap around cylindrical objects like woodwind instruments.
